I waited six months to write this review because I did not want my anger or my grief to be the reason it was written. Time has passed, the employee who made the decision that day has been let go, and still this needs to be said. I lost my beloved dog, Sir-Lix-Alot, and nothing will ever bring him back.
Sir-Lix-Alot was an 11-year-old terrier mix. Years ago, I was told he had an irregular heartbeat and an enlarged heart. We monitored it as he aged. At his senior wellness visit, he was scheduled for an X-ray to check the size of his heart. That appointment was on a Friday. I was told he did not need medication yet, only that he needed to lose a little weight.
The following Monday, around 4:30 p.m., after picking my son up from school, I came home and immediately knew something was wrong. Sir-Lix-Alot was not in his usual spot. He was wheezing and coughing. When you know your pet, you know.
I called the office and asked if I could bring Sir-Lix-Alot in immediately. We live three minutes away. This had been his vet since the day he walked into my backyard and into my life nine years earlier. I was told no. The person who answered did not ask a veterinarian, did not ask if anyone could see him, and did not try to help. She told me it was too late in the day and that if something was really wrong, I should take him to an emergency vet. My mother also called and begged them to let us bring Sir-Lix-Alot in. She was also turned away.
I picked up Sir-Lix-Alot, and my eight-year-old son got into the backseat after seeing how upset I was. We had to drive past this very clinic on the way to the emergency vet. There were cars in the parking lot. They were not closed.
Sir-Lix-Alot lay still in my lap until we were about a mile from the emergency vet. Then he suddenly lifted his head, began coughing, blood came from his mouth, he urinated on me, and he went limp. He died in my arms.
I was hysterical. My son witnessed all of this. I ran into the emergency clinic with Sir-Lix-Alot in my arms, begging them to save him. They restarted his heart, but fluid continued to come up, and there was no saving him. I then had to make the decision to euthanize Sir-Lix-Alot. My mother arrived shortly after and paid a $1,200 bill for restarting his heart and then stopping it again.
The next day, I emailed this clinic to tell them what happened and that I blamed them for turning us away. About a week later, the office manager called and told me the employee who refused to see us had been let go. I was told that next time I should “just come in.” I blame myself for not doing that, but when you are told no, twice, you listen.
I will never know if Sir-Lix-Alot could have been saved. I will never know what was missed or what went wrong so suddenly with my otherwise happy, loving dog. I will live with those questions for the rest of my life.
The photo attached is Sir-Lix-Alot’s urn. That is what I was sent home with.

Avoid this vet unless you want stress, confusion, and unnecessary complications.

This clinic constantly introduces new staff members, which suggests poor internal culture, inadequate compensation, or a failure to hire and retain qualified professionals. The result is inconsistent care and frequent miscommunication that directly affects your pet.

They once operated on the wrong leg of my dog. That level of error is inexcusable under any circumstances. Still, I chose to give them the benefit of the doubt. They comped both surgeries, and I took it as a serious but isolated mistake. I continued using their services because I wanted to believe they could improve. But they have shown again and again that they cannot be trusted to get the basics right.

Their communication failures are routine. I recently called twice to confirm the procedure for collecting a urine sample due to an ongoing issue. On the first call, we were told to bring in a sample in a sterile jar. That did not align with what we recalled from speaking with the doctor previously. We called again to clarify. They repeated the same instructions and assured us it was correct.

Wanting to do everything properly, I traveled in to pick up a sterile container directly from the clinic to avoid any confusion or contamination. Only during the in-person consultation did it become clear that their instructions had been completely wrong. What was actually required was a direct collection from the bladder using a needle—a procedure that only they could perform.

Because of this misinformation, we had to leave our dog at the clinic and make a second trip after he produced enough urine for the correct method. This was entirely avoidable and wasted both time and effort.

On that same visit, they claimed to have administered his monthly Librela shot. I confirmed this with the vet tech when I dropped him off, and again with the doctor when I picked him up. However, there was no record of it, and I was not charged for the service. That leaves me with no way to confirm whether it was actually done.

They also show no sense of urgency. A widely available generic prescription that an urgent care clinic filled within minutes took this clinic more than twenty-four hours to process, with no follow-up and no explanation.

This is not just about one mistake. It is about repeated failures, wasted time, and a clear pattern of negligence.

This clinic is careless, disorganized, and unreliable. If you value your time, your money, and more importantly your pet’s well-being, go elsewhere.

UPDATE: We ended up taking our dog to the DVSC (Dallas Veterinary Surgical Center) and they were very concerned. After examining him they confirmed that the issue was with the same knee that NDVH operated on! They dug into his surgery for us and found that the surgeon who operated was NOT BOARD CERTIFIED. We had to pay another $4000 for another surgery where they found that his meniscus was also torn.... the original surgeon did not catch nor fix that so now we are out of pocket even more. We did not even know that non-board certified surgeons were a thing considering for humans this is not the case, but the DVSC told us that NDVH should have informed us that our surgeon was non-board certified and given us the option. The irony is that the surgery through the DVSC would have been LESS money with a board certified surgeon than it was through NDVH with a non-board certified surgeon. Lesson learned!!!!

This place has seriously gone down hill. As you will see from other recent reviews, all of their previous Veterinarians are now gone, without notice. This includes the one that diagnosed our dog recently, AND the one who performed surgery on the same dog. Now that the surgery did not take, the new Veterinarian is blowing off our concerns, finger pointing to the old vets that are nowhere to be found, and she even started laughing when I explained our concerns. Go somewhere else! More details below...

Our 8 year old dog who was in perfect health did hurt his knee. Based on the directive of this practice, they said it was only a partial tear and would be premature to operate on the knee. Within 1 week he fully tore the other knee. When we took him back, they told us this was typical if the original knee isn't operated on - then why did they tell us not to operate?! We ended up paying $5000 to fix he now fully torn knee (second knee). Within months he is back to limping and putting no weight on the second knee (the one we operated on). When we took him back for them to review their own surgery, they charged us another $600!!! They told us that even though he was limping on the knee that had surgery, it was really the problem of the original knee, and recommend we pay another $5000 for another surgery. Then told us that even then, he will not have the same quality of life because now he has developed chronic arthritis because they never operated on the original knee in the first place!! When I pushed back on the doctor she literally laughed. I will forever regret taking our dog to this practice and now will always wonder "what if?" we hadn't take him here in the first place.

I had seen multiple warnings in local neighborhood posts about how this vet clinic has gone majorly downhill. However, since we’ve always had such positive experiences in the past, we decided to give it another try. Unfortunately, it confirmed what others have been saying.

We had a drop-off appointment this morning, and I sat in the lobby waiting. I watched another vet’s technician kindly and efficiently bring in patient after patient. Meanwhile, no one came for our dog. After 20 minutes, I checked in at the front desk to make sure we hadn’t been missed and was told someone would be right out. I waited another 10 minutes — now a total of 30 minutes — and still, no one came.

At that point, we left. It’s sad to see a once-great local vet decline like this. I think there’s a reason all the good vets have bailed. I now have to agree with everyone else — stay away. There are much better, more reliable options out there.

I've been a loyal client of North Dallas Veterinary Hospital for over 25 years, as have my family and friends. But I have to ask—where have all the long-time veterinarians gone? Dr. Washatka, Dr. Hudson, Dr. Finney, Dr. Nichols and others—what happened? Why weren’t we notified?

Having known Dr. Ford since before he started this clinic at this location, I know he put great thought into selecting veterinarians who were truly amazing. The team he built was exceptional, which makes this sudden change even more disappointing.

For those of us who consider our pets family, the disappearance of trusted veterinarians without any communication is deeply upsetting. Transparency and respect for long-time clients should be a priority. The lack of notice feels unprofessional and disheartening.

If there was a change, we deserved to be informed. I sincerely hope the clinic will address this and improve communication moving forward.

I had a terrible experience at [Veterinary Hospital NORTH DALLAS VETERINARY EMERGENCY HOSPITAL They started treating my pet without doing any blood or urine tests, jumping straight to expensive treatments without even knowing what was wrong.
After three days with no improvement, we asked for answers, and shockingly, they admitted they didn’t know the cause of my pet’s condition. Despite their lack of proper diagnosis, they still charged me an outrageous amount.

is unacceptable. Pet owners trust vets to care for their animals, not to guess at treatments and rack up bills. I would strongly advise others to avoid this hospital and seek care elsewhere. Save yourself the stress, expense, and heartache.
